destroy_phase.dead_branch: the duplicate-found path tests whether the write cursor equals the old end after subtracting 0x10; that test cannot be true because the read cursor never passes the old end, so the branch is dead
destroy_phase.duplicates: duplicate copies beyond new_end are never disposed; their storage is abandoned with the freed buffer
destroy_phase.per_element: call the element +0x08 qword as a function with the element +0x00 qword as argument, in array order
destroy_phase.range: [begin, new_end) where new_end is one past the last kept element; on the no-duplicate path new_end is the old end

element_layout.+0x00: argument qword passed to the disposer
element_layout.+0x08: disposer function pointer, called with the +0x00 qword

free_phase.buffer: when +0x28 is non-null, operator delete(+0x28, +0x38 minus +0x28)
free_phase.not_cleared: the routine never writes +0x28, +0x30 or +0x38 after freeing; +0x30 was set to begin in the reset phase on the flag-set path
free_phase.tail: tail jump to 0x61bd0e0 (FDE pc=0x61bd0e0..0x61bd131) with the object pointer in rdi; its body is not pinned here

gates.empty_range: begin equal to end on the flag-set path: sort, unique and destroy phases skipped; reset and virtual phases still run
gates.flag_clear: flag byte zero: skip sort, unique, destroy, reset and virtual phases; free the buffer if non-null, then tail-jump
gates.flag_set: flag byte nonzero: flag cleared first, then the full clear runs

object_layout.+0x00: head function pointer (called only on the flag-set path; null skips the call and also skips the chain walk)
object_layout.+0x08: first argument for the head call
object_layout.+0x10: second argument for the head call
object_layout.+0x18: chain head pointer (linked list; each node has its own +0x08/+0x10 args and +0x18 next)
object_layout.+0x20: flag byte; zero selects the free-only path, nonzero selects the full clear
object_layout.+0x28: pair-array begin pointer (null skips the buffer free)
object_layout.+0x30: pair-array end pointer (reset to begin by the clear)
object_layout.+0x38: pair-array capacity end (delete size is +0x38 minus +0x28)

reset_phase.end: pair-array end (+0x30) is set to begin when it differs; on the empty path it already equals begin so nothing is written

routine.returns: never returns normally; tail-jumps to 0x61bd0e0 with the object pointer

sort_phase.depth_argument: 2 times floor(log2(element_count)) for element_count >= 1, computed with bsr; the literal -2 left in rdx when the byte count is below 16
sort_phase.first_call: callee 0x5d4a3f0 with (begin, end, depth); body not pinned here
sort_phase.inlined_insertion_sort: ascending order by unsigned (first qword, second qword); each later pair is shifted left over larger pairs until its slot is found; the inner walk has no lower-bound check
sort_phase.large_range: byte count above 0x100: callee 0x5d497e0 with (begin, begin + 0x100), then the inlined insertion sort below over [begin + 0x100, end)
sort_phase.shape_note: the call pattern (full-range callee, then first-16 or whole-small-range callee, then an unguarded insertion tail) matches a final-insertion-sort shape; that identification is inference, the pinned facts are the call sites, arguments and the inlined loop
sort_phase.small_range: byte count at most 0x100 (16 elements): callee 0x5d497e0 with (begin, end); body not pinned here

unique_phase.compaction: write cursor starts at the first element of the first duplicate pair; later pairs differing from the last kept pair (either qword) are copied forward in order; pairs equal to the last kept pair are skipped
unique_phase.kept_set: exactly one copy of each distinct pair, in sorted order
unique_phase.no_duplicate: scan reaches the end with no duplicate: every element is kept
unique_phase.scan: walks adjacent pairs from the second element; the first pair whose both qwords equal its predecessor is the first duplicate
unique_phase.single_element: range of one element: that element is kept

unknowns: Bodies of the sort-phase callees 0x5d4a3f0 and 0x5d497e0 and of the tail callee 0x61bd0e0; only their call sites and arguments are pinned.
Identities of the head, chain-node and element-disposer callees and the element type names; only the call protocol is pinned.
The purpose behind disposing each distinct pair exactly once in sorted order; the disposal order and the once-each rule are observed, the reason is not claimed.
Behavior when the pair-array byte count is not a multiple of 16; the depth literal -2 for a sub-16-byte count is pinned, nothing further is claimed.

virtual_phase.chain: only after a non-null head call: for each node from +0x18 while non-null: call the node function pointer with (node +0x08, node +0x10), then operator delete(node, 0x20), then advance to node +0x18
virtual_phase.clearing: afterwards +0x00 is zeroed and +0x18 is zeroed
virtual_phase.head: when +0x00 is non-null, call it with (+0x08, +0x10)
virtual_phase.skipped_on: the flag-clear path never runs this phase and never zeroes +0x00 or +0x18
virtual_phase.null_head: a null +0x00 at 0x5d505a4 jumps straight to 0x5d505e4, which zeroes +0x00 and +0x18 WITHOUT walking the chain: the chain nodes are neither called nor deleted, they are abandoned under the zeroed pointer
